Hence, users can store in RTC memory a program for the ULP coprocessor to access RTC peripherals, internal sensors, and RTC registers during Deep-sleep.
In power-sensitive scenarios, the main CPU goes to sleep mode to lower power consumption.
Meanwhile, the coprocessor is woken up by ULP timer, and then monitors the external environment or interacts with the external circuit by controlling peripherals such as RTC GPIO, RTC
The coprocessor wakes the main CPU up once a wakeup condition is reached.
ESP32-S3 has two ULP coprocessors, with one based on RISC-V instruction set architecture (ULP-RISC-V) and the other on finite state machine (ULP-FSM).
Users can choose between the two coprocessors depending on their needs.
